title: SO-F-09.3 Finding model for organisational intelligence: a finding is a graph claim capped at theory by evidence, promoted to fact only by a person or a verification, with dismissal, correction and adjudication events and no disclosure beyond the reader's permissions
request: Version 3 of this spec, which supersedes SO-F-09.2 (signed as contract k-so-f-09-2-finding-model--e25d9e; the SO-F-09.2 spec file is unchanged and stays on record, and the manifest and RECONCILIATION mark it superseded by this spec). Reason: owner delegation, 1 Nov 2026: SO-F-09.2 makes the credential-bound entry point Graph.bindFindingEvent set 'by' from the resolved credential, but raw Graph.applyOp and the replay of the op log still take data.by as written, so a forged by on a record that went around the entry point counts as the subject it names; pull request #362 documents this as open and says it must close before any writer calls bindFindingEvent. Accepted decisions: (a) a secret-free credential descriptor on the record is the trust carrier; the log is only as trusted as its writer, because a writer that builds the descriptor from caller input defeats it, and signing the log is a separate decision that stays out of this spec; (b) the descriptor is a top-level field of the record, rec.credential, and not a field of rec.data: data stays caller input and is ignored for authority. New definition 5 (below) and nine new criteria pin it. The scope adds src/engine/oplog.mjs and test/oplog.test.mjs; src/engine/vault.mjs and src/engine/tokens.mjs stay out of scope, so this spec builds no writer, and nothing writes a finding operation yet. Every requirement, criterion and scope entry of SO-F-09.2 is kept, and its 20 criteria are carried verbatim. ADR 8 (trust governance in the federated model) is proposed and not decided, in pull request #371 and not on main; the descriptor is the shape resolveActor already accepts today, so this spec does not decide the trust root, and the trust carrier may change when ADR 8 is decided. The request text of SO-F-09.2 follows unchanged. Version 2 of this spec, which supersedes SO-F-09 (signed as contract k-so-f-09-finding-model-fo-cbe213, version 2, which superseded the first signed version; the SO-F-09 spec file is unchanged and stays on record, and the manifest and RECONCILIATION mark it superseded by this spec). Reason: owner delegation, 1 Nov 2026: the lead accepted four definitions that the text of SO-F-09 leaves open (a stub session; who may write a verification record; where the 'by' field comes from; how withholding works) and they are written into the contract and pinned with criteria; the scope adds only src/engine/identity.mjs, which definition 3 needs; docs/MODULES.md and changelog.d/SO-F-09.md are already in the signed scope and are not added again. Accepted definitions: (1) A stub session is an agent subject or a raw status op: neither can promote a finding to fact, by a logged status change, an adjudication, a verification or evidence. (2) A verification record may be written by a person, operator or service subject; it takes effect only when its result is a pass, and a record from an agent or with a failed result is kept and changes nothing. (3) The 'by' field of an event is set from the resolved credential (SO-F-01), never from caller input: through the credential-bound entry point a caller-supplied 'by' is ignored, so a forged by of person:x on an adjudication or service:x on a verification makes no finding a fact, and an agent credential in the personal scope resolves to an agent subject, not to person:owner. (4) Withholding is strict: if any source of a finding is withheld from the reader, the whole statement is withheld, with the reasons and corrections in its history and every entity or owner drawn from a withheld source, and an entity or owner with no source (source null) is withheld from every partial view; the reader sees only how many sources are withheld. Provisional: who may adjudicate (a person), who may verify (a person, operator or service), who may dismiss (a person or an operator subject only, by the safe default of ADR 5 that what is ungated stays denied; an agent or a service subject cannot dismiss) and the two adjudication outcomes, confirm and reject, are provisional until the permission matrix (ADR 5, open, in docs/scope-one/DECISIONS.md) and the decision and blocker workflow (SO-A-05) are decided; they are kept in one table so that deciding them changes one place. Pull request #362 builds this contract (head fe3d7f3, stacked on #349). Every requirement, criterion and scope entry of SO-F-09 is kept. Build layer of the Scope One programme, adapted from the unsigned fold of 30 Oct 2026 (fold id SO-F-09) and validated against memev main at d1c65ef. Contracts marked with a dagger are signed in the owner's vault and are not visible in this repository; they are cited by id only. Implements the design records SO-2.04 (Cross-project intelligence: evidence-backed discovery across otherwise independent work); SO-2.01 (Organisational knowledge model: relationships between people, teams, projects, decisions, artefacts and evidence) (contracts/scope-one/specs). The decision record cites this contract by id and keeps only the gaps this one does not cover. Memev contracts that land first: SO-F-01, SO-F-02. Page: docs/ORGANISATIONAL-INTELLIGENCE.md comes from the federation architecture documentation (PR #223, branch docs/federation-architecture, not on main); until that merges, the first contract to need a page creates it with its Status section, labelled planned or architectural target, and the later ones extend it. Source in the fold: #222 section 13.6 (evidence-led and cautious; dismissal and correction) and #223 ORGANISATIONAL-INTELLIGENCE.md (evidence and authority). Settled decisions this contract follows (owner decision 31 Oct 2026, docs/scope-one/DECISIONS.md): topology is local-first and the cloud is only a relay and a backup; every supported provider stands on equal footing and no work or tier depends on one; crdt-merge is reached only through the provider boundary of src/engine/merge.mjs (docs/EXTENSION-POINTS.md) and this contract adds no merge engine to the core; tiers follow docs/PRICING.md (Free core, Personal for up to 3 computers with no per-computer add-on, higher tiers by contacting us) with no Personal trial; the git backup keeps running every few minutes (sync.interval_min). Memory authority: ADR 7 (memory and project-state authority) is proposed in PR #325 and is not decided here; this contract cites it and the local-first decision, and keeps one store under the vault with no second database. Provenance: adapted from the unsigned fold of 30 Oct 2026. Changes: (1) converted from the vault task format to the memev spec format (named tests run as red-green checks on the own test file of the contract; inline regular expression flags became the flags key; hygiene and decision verifiers became commands or doc checks). (2) removed fold-only fields and the owner-decision marker field, reworded the stop rule that named a patent, and made the text pass the leak scan. (3) The fold said the graph holds claims with status fact, theory and conjecture; src/engine/graph.mjs has five (fact, theory, conjecture, contested, refuted). The cap applies to promotion to fact; contested and refuted stand as the graph derives them. (4) Boundary with PG-10.1 WP10-01 and WP10-02 (knowledge status lattice and status fields): the lattice of a fact is owned there. This contract defines only what a finding is and its cap, and maps the cap into the lattice (at most corroborated) once it lands.

tasks.description: The intelligence layer should not become an unbounded inference engine. The graph (src/engine/graph.mjs) already holds claims with status (fact, theory, conjecture, contested, refuted) and provenance, promoted and demoted as evidence arrives. A finding is such a claim with source event links, affected entities, scope and time context and confidence, whose evidence-derived status is capped at theory; fact needs a person's event or a verification record; ordinary claims keep today's rule. Conflict detection, precision and recall and decision routing are SO-F-13. Definitions accepted 1 Nov 2026: (1) A stub session is an agent subject or a raw status op: neither can promote a finding to fact, by a logged status change, an adjudication, a verification or evidence. (2) A verification record may be written by a person, operator or service subject; it takes effect only when its result is a pass, and a record from an agent or with a failed result is kept and changes nothing. (3) The 'by' field of an event is set from the resolved credential (SO-F-01), never from caller input: through the credential-bound entry point a caller-supplied 'by' is ignored, so a forged by of person:x on an adjudication or service:x on a verification makes no finding a fact, and an agent credential in the personal scope resolves to an agent subject, not to person:owner. (4) Withholding is strict: if any source of a finding is withheld from the reader, the whole statement is withheld, with the reasons and corrections in its history and every entity or owner drawn from a withheld source, and an entity or owner with no source (source null) is withheld from every partial view; the reader sees only how many sources are withheld. Provisional: who may adjudicate (a person), who may verify (a person, operator or service), who may dismiss (a person or an operator subject only, by the safe default of ADR 5 that what is ungated stays denied; an agent or a service subject cannot dismiss) and the two adjudication outcomes, confirm and reject, are provisional until the permission matrix (ADR 5, open, in docs/scope-one/DECISIONS.md) and the decision and blocker workflow (SO-A-05) are decided; they are kept in one table so that deciding them changes one place. Definition accepted 1 Nov 2026 (5): the effective actor of a finding operation is derived from the credential descriptor of its own record, never from data.by. (i) A finding operation is a record of type claim.finding or one of FINDING_EVENTS. It carries rec.credential, a top-level field of the record next to agent and client, and not a field of rec.data. (ii) rec.credential is a plain, secret-free descriptor in the shape resolveActor already accepts today: a verified credential given as id, identity_scope and subject, or a role binding given as role and principal with the scope it was issued for. It holds no token secret and no key material. (iii) Graph.bindFindingEvent returns the descriptor of the actor it was given, next to type and data, for a writer to append; it is built from the actor and never from the caller's data. (iv) Graph.applyOp, and so the replay of the op log which calls it, resolves rec.credential through resolveActor at the record's own time (rec.ts), and the subject it resolves to is the effective by: stored as raised_by, as the history by and as the decision by. data.by is ignored for authority and is overwritten, so a forged by of person:x or service:x on a record of an agent credential makes no finding a fact. (v) A finding operation with no rec.credential, with one that does not resolve, or with one whose subject is revoked or expired at rec.ts changes nothing in the graph: it is not applied, and it leaves no history entry. It fails closed. (vi) src/engine/oplog.mjs persists rec.credential when an operation carries one and adds the key only then, so a record without one is byte for byte what it was and its hash is unchanged; oplog.mjs does not name claim.finding, admitFinding, bindFindingEvent or FINDING_EVENTS, which stay in src/engine/graph.mjs. (vii) Trust: the descriptor is a trust carrier and is not authenticated. The op log is as trusted as its writer, and a writer that builds rec.credential from caller input defeats this definition; the writer is future work and is not built here, and it must set rec.credential from the result of bindFindingEvent. Signing or authenticating log records is a separate decision and is not in this spec. (viii) The trust carrier may change when ADR 8 (trust governance in the federated model, proposed, pull request #371) is decided, and when the operation envelope of PG-04.1 (docs/OPERATION-ENVELOPE.md, its authorisation field) replaces the op-log record; the descriptor is only the shape resolveActor accepts today. resolveRequest and resolveActor are unchanged. (ix) Uniform refusal of a taken id: a raise through bindFindingEvent whose id is already a claim gets one refusal, the same code and the same text, whether that claim is a finding the actor may reach, a finding in a scope the actor may not reach, or an ordinary claim, and the text does not carry anything of that claim; it is the uniform refusal that bindFindingEvent already gives for a finding it does not reach, so a raise is not an oracle for the ids of other scopes (src/engine/graph.mjs, admitFinding). Out of scope: whether a reader who can read only some of a finding's sources may adjudicate, verify or dismiss it, that is, a partial reader deciding blind, is an ADR 5 (permission matrix) decision and stays out of this spec; nothing here changes who may decide.

stop_rules: Stop and post BLOCKED when a criterion cannot pass without weakening a test, skipping a test or relaxing an assertion.
Stop and ask when the work would name a client product, a person, a server or a seat in repository text; the client names live in docs/CLIENTS.md only.
Stop when the work would add a runtime dependency, a model call, a network call at install or start, a second store for project state, or any reporting that is not opt-in and off by default.
Stop when the work would move convergence logic into the core, vendor the engine, or add a merge engine beside the provider boundary of src/engine/merge.mjs.

Stop when the work would implement a federation, replication, trust, admission or computation feature beyond the specification, schema, validator and conformance test the contract names; the product keeps the planned label on it.
If any criterion fails after the fix: STOP, report the measured result, the failing check and file:line. Do not start the next task.
If the work needs a path outside scope: STOP and ask the owner to amend the contract. Never widen scope silently.
Stop when the work would decide whether a partial reader may adjudicate, verify or dismiss a finding it cannot read in full: that is an ADR 5 decision and stays out of this spec.
Stop when the work would sign, hash-chain or encrypt log records, add a key store, or authenticate rec.credential: signing the log is a separate decision and is not in this spec.
Stop when the work needs src/engine/vault.mjs or src/engine/tokens.mjs: the writer is not part of this spec, so ask the owner for a separate contract.
Stop when the work would change resolveRequest, the signed SO-F-01 tests, or the 20 criteria carried from SO-F-09.2.
